text.p: The following are the reports carried by Lithanian newspapers on Thursady. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Belarus President Aleksander Lukashenko is not afraid to be called a dictator. "I like being the president of Belarus," Lukshenko told the newspaper.
- Lithuanian national television has been used for two years illegally to produce advertising programmes for competitors.
- Bourse trade was dominated by government T-bills.
- Canadian company Bombardier demonstrated its new Canadian Regional Jet series 200ER to Lithuania's transpot mnistry oficials.

- Lithuanian experts say the wish of Siemens to devalue the litas by nearly two times is unprofessional and arrogant. The German company last week said it intended to cut investment in Lithuania as the currency was overvalued.

- The ruling Homeland Union faction in parliament wants to oust the prosecutor general from his post by a no-confidence vote. Vladas Nikitinas sent his resignation letter to President Algirdas Brazauskas but the president did not accept it.
- Klaipeda sea port was reopened on Wednesday after it was closed because of storm Tuesday night.
- Hermis Bank's shareholders decided to boost its share capital by 23 million litas to 90 million litas. The biggest part of the shares is to distributed abroad.
- A World Bank mission approves of the government decision to close problem-struck Innovation Bank and programmes to privatise state-owned commercial banks.
- The Russian embassy in Vilnius refused to pass the cangratulation letter of parliament's chairman Vytauatas Lansbergis to new Chechen president Aslan Maschadov.
